examInfo.group: 大學組第一、二、三、四類組
examInfo.title: 115學年度身心障礙學生升學大專校院甄試 英文

questions.text: The email that you send will ______ back if the address is incorrect.
steps: 「bounce back」是固定搭配，指信件因地址錯誤被退回（電子郵件退信）。transfer(轉移)、grasp(抓住)、attach(附加)皆不符合語意。

questions.text: Jenny paused for a moment in ______ before answering the difficult question.
steps: 「in hesitation」意為「猶豫地」，符合「停頓片刻」的語境。harmony(和諧)、leisure(悠閒)、volume(音量)皆與語境不符。

questions.text: Mr. Lin has some ______ plans for his new coffee business. More than ten chain stores are scheduled to open next month.
steps: 下個月要開超過十家連鎖店，顯示計畫「雄心勃勃」，ambitious(有野心的)最符合語意。durable(耐用的)、fluent(流利的)、circular(circular的)皆不符。

questions.text: Students in this school are encouraged to ______ the Internet for study purposes in the science class.
steps: 「access the Internet」是固定用法，意為「使用／連上網路」。dismiss(解散)、encounter(遭遇)、target(以...為目標)皆不符合語境。

questions.text: Rise of property values in Taiwan has been so ______ that many people cannot afford housing.
steps: 房價上漲到讓許多人買不起房子，顯示漲幅「劇烈、顯著」，dramatic(劇烈的)最符合。fragile(脆弱的)、pessimistic(悲觀的)、fashionable(流行的)皆不符。

questions.text: More than 70,000 people have been killed in the Gaza War since 2023. It’s a big human ______.
steps: 大量人員死亡是「人道悲劇」，tragedy(悲劇)最符合語境。protest(抗議)、suicide(自殺)、caution(謹慎)皆不符。

questions.text: The U.S. state of Maine experienced severe winter storms ______ by low temperatures, strong winds, and significant snowfall.
steps: 「characterized by」意為「以...為特徵」，暴風雪以低溫、強風、大雪為特徵，語意通順。monitored(被監控)、frustrated(受挫)、justified(被證實合理)皆不符。

questions.text: Chen Ning Yang, a ______ researcher in physics, was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1957.
steps: 獲得諾貝爾獎的物理學家應是「傑出、知名」的研究者，prominent(卓越的、傑出的)最符合。consistent(一致的)、definite(明確的)、genetic(基因的)皆不符。

questions.text: Suffering from stage ______, Steve always feels a panic and forgets his lines in front of an audience.
steps: 「stage fright」是固定片語，意為「怯場」，符合「在觀眾面前恐慌、忘詞」的語境。

questions.text: Attracted by the interesting new group project, the students started ______, but they soon got bored and lost interest.
steps: 對照後半句「很快就感到無聊失去興趣」，前半句應是「熱情地開始」形成對比，enthusiastically(熱情地)最符合。apparently(顯然地)、identically(相同地)、moderately(適度地)皆不符語境對比。

questions.text: （空格 11）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 前句說「運動有益健康是常識」，本句要表達「較少人知道園藝的角色」，形成語意轉折，But(但是)最符合。

questions.text: 【11-15題組】Gardeners might be delighted to learn that the number of calories burned from 30 minutes of gardening is ＿＿(12)＿＿ playing badminton or practicing yoga.
steps: 「be comparable to」意為「與...相當」，表示園藝燃燒的卡路里與打羽球或做瑜伽相當，語意通順。turned into(變成)、prior to(在...之前)、counting on(依靠)皆不符。

questions.text: （空格 13）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 「as part of their diets」意為「作為飲食的一部分」，符合「將蔬果納入日常飲食」的語意。

questions.text: （空格 14）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 後面舉例「薰衣草治輕度憂鬱、薑治頭痛」屬於列舉「某些」療法，Some(一些)最符合，且主詞需對應複數可數概念（一些療法/植物）。

questions.text: 【11-15題組】those who garden every day have wellbeing ＿＿(15)＿＿ 6.6% higher and stress levels 4.2% lower than people who do not garden at all.
steps: 「wellbeing scores」意為「幸福感分數」，與後面「6.6% higher」的百分比數據搭配最合理，指幸福感量表分數較高。

questions.text: （空格 16）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 利用星象與地標「判定」船隻位置，determine(判定、確定)最符合語意。

questions.text: （空格 17）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 「feeling the flow of currents」意為「感受洋流的流動」，flow(流動)最符合航海導航的語境。

questions.text: （空格 18）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 逗號後接非限定關係子句，修飾前面整個概念（對自然世界的深刻理解），須用which，that不可接在逗號後引導非限定關係子句。

questions.text: （空格 19）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 指南針使得「即使天候能見度不佳」時導航仍然「可行」，possible(可能的、可行的)最符合語意。

questions.text: （空格 20）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 讓水手能夠規劃行程並「想像、視覺化」預定路線，visualize(將...視覺化)最符合語意。recite(背誦)、guard(守衛)、contribute(貢獻)皆不符。

questions.text: Which of the following states the purpose of the passage?

options.B: To show the way of self-protection.
options.C: To explain the difficulty of achieving collaboration.
options.D: To demonstrate the use of strategies to win a lawsuit.

steps: 全文透過囚徒困境理論，說明個人利益與集體利益衝突時，人們往往難以達成合作（即使合作對雙方最有利），並以氣候談判為例呼應此困境，主旨在於解釋「達成合作的困難」。
questions.final: 答案：(C) To explain the difficulty of achieving collaboration.

questions.text: What does the phrase “the same way” mean in the first paragraph?
steps: 原句「when two individuals act in their own self-interest, they would both experience worse outcomes due to the other behaving in the same way」，「the same way」指的正是前面提到的「act in their own self-interest」，即「服務自己的利益」。
questions.final: 答案：(D) Serving one's own interests.

questions.text: According to the example mentioned in the passage, what would the prisoners most probably get?

options.A: One being sentenced one year and the other five years.
options.B: One being set free and the other sentenced ten years.
options.C: Both being put in jail for five years.

steps: 囚徒困境的核心正是「雙方都因自利而背叛對方」，導致雙方各判五年（次佳結果），而非合作沉默各判一年（最佳結果）。文章強調「他們更可能背叛對方以逃避懲罰」，故最可能的結果是兩人都被判五年。
questions.final: 答案：(C) Both being put in jail for five years.

questions.text: What light does the prisoner’s dilemma shed on climate talks in the last paragraph?

options.A: The necessity of cooperation for decreasing greenhouse gases.
options.B: The risk of disclosing damages caused by climate change.
options.C: The benefit of solving problems through negotiation.
options.D: The need of regulations to protect the environment.

steps: 末段說明若所有國家在氣候談判中合作減排，長期而言對大家都更有利，呼應囚徒困境「合作才是最佳結果」的核心概念，強調的是「合作對減少溫室氣體排放的必要性」。
questions.final: 答案：(A) The necessity of cooperation for decreasing greenhouse gases.

questions.text: What does “the burden” in the last paragraph refer to?

options.D: The work of conserving natural resources.

steps: 原句引述數學家的話：「每個國家都希望全球減排，但更希望是別人承擔這個負擔」，「the burden」指的正是前面提到的「emission reductions」（減排的負擔），即「溫室氣體排放的削減」。
questions.final: 答案：(B) The reduction of gas emissions.

p11_15.title: 11-15 題組
p11_15.html:
It’s common knowledge that exercise is good for you.　＿＿(11)＿＿ less known is the role that gardening can play in helping to keep you fit and healthy. Gardeners might be delighted to learn that the number of calories burned from 30 minutes of gardening is
＿＿(12)＿＿ playing badminton or practicing yoga. In addition, growing and eating their own fruit and vegetables, gardeners are more likely to include food produce ＿＿(13)＿＿ their diets.
Gardening has a long history connected to medicine. For centuries, gardens have been a source not only of food on the table but also remedies to treat common ailments. ＿＿(14)＿＿ , such as lavenders for mild depression and gingers for headaches, have been embraced by people today. It is increasingly acknowledged that plants and green spaces are associated with better physical and mental health. In 2021, the RHS, the UK’s gardening charity, released research that revealed those who garden every day have wellbeing ＿＿(15)＿＿ 6.6% higher and stress levels 4.2% lower than people who do not garden at all. Nowadays, as the population ages and healthcare costs increase, gardening that promotes health and happiness has a renewed importance.

p16_20.title: 16-20 題組
p16_20.html:
For thousands of years, sailors have used different methods and tools to navigate the open seas safely. From using stars and other natural landmarks to　＿＿(16)＿＿　the position of their ships, to modern technology such as GPS, the industry has continuously looked for better ways to navigate with increased accuracy.
One of the earliest known forms of open-ocean navigation was likely practiced by the Polynesians. They were the masters of ancient navigation, using the stars, feeling the ＿＿(17)＿＿ of currents, observing seabirds and cloud formation to find new islands. Over time, the knowledge of these early navigators grew, and an insightful view was developed of the natural world, ＿＿(18)＿＿ allowed them to navigate thousands of miles.
These observational methods later evolved into more complex techniques and devices. One of the significant developments was the invention of the compass. It was a directional tool that made navigation　＿＿(19)＿＿ even when weather and visibility was poor. Another key development was the use of maps or nautical charts in navigation. Books were written that included directions to navigate between ports based on landmarks and ocean currents, allowing sailors to plan their journey and to ＿＿(20)＿＿ their intended route. Sailors were able to choose the best course to reach their destination in long-distance voyages.

p21_25.title: 21-25 題組
p21_25.html:
The prisoner’s dilemma is a theory that describes the behavior of human beings and the consequences in choosing between individual and collective interests. It presents a situation where two persons can either cooperate for mutual benefit or betray their partner for individual gain. According to the theory, when two individuals act in their own self-interest, they would both experience worse outcomes due to the other behaving in the same way.
A classic example of a prisoner’s dilemma is a game between two prisoners. Prisoner A and Prisoner B are caught by the police and are held in separate cells for questioning. Each is given a choice between betraying the other or staying quiet. Neither knows what the other will do, but the outcome depends on their combined choices. There are three possible outcomes:
1. One prisoner betrays the other and confesses the crime while the other stays
quiet in the hope of cooperating to conceal the crime. As a result, the betrayer
is set free but the silent prisoner gets a heavy sentence of ten years.
2. Both stay quiet, and each gets a lighter sentence of one year.
3. Each betrays the other and confesses the crime, and each gets a moderate
sentence of five years.
The best possible outcome for both prisoners is to cooperate with each other and get a one-year sentence, but they would more likely betray the other to escape punishment. The case shows that in the face of the conflict between selfish interest and mutual benefit, if each individual goes after their own self-interest, the outcome is worse than if they had both cooperated.
The prisoner’s dilemma finds application in diverse areas, including environmental issues. According to mathematician Peter Wood, an inherent prisoner’s dilemma arises when addressing greenhouse gas emissions, because “every country wants global emission reductions, but would prefer that someone else take on the burden.” If all nations involved in climate change negotiations worked together and committed to the end goal of emission reduction, they would be better off in terms of long-term benefits. However, most negotiations are not kept up because there are always short-term economic benefits for a country to break agreements and avoid responsibility.
